Vancouver, BC – TheNewswire - September 10, 2026 – Critical Infrastructure Technologies Ltd.

(FRA: X9V) (“CiTech” or the “Company”), a leading developer of autonomous, high-capacity mobile communications and security platforms, is pleased to announce that it has executed a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") with Wojskowe Zaklady Motoryzacyjne S.A. ("WZM") and H. Cegielski-Poznan S.A. ("HCP"), establishing a strategic framework for the development, localisation and commercialisation of CiTech's Nexus 20 autonomous platform in Poland and across agreed markets in Central and Eastern Europe.

The MOU, dated 9 September 2026, builds on the Letter of Intent entered into by the parties on 18 February 2026 and represents a significant step forward in CiTech's strategy to establish a long-term industrial and market presence in Poland.

Under the MOU, CiTech and the Polish Partners intend to work together to develop Poland as a manufacturing, assembly, integration, maintenance and support base for Nexus 20 platforms, while supporting opportunities with the Polish Armed Forces and other approved customers across Poland, Central and Eastern Europe and the broader NATO Eastern Flank.
The strategic cooperation is intended to include:
local assembly and integration of Nexus 20 platforms in Poland;
integration of communications, surveillance and other mission-specific systems;
testing, quality assurance and commissioning;
maintenance, repair, overhaul and lifecycle support;
development of Polish sourcing and supply-chain capability;
appropriate technology transfer, technical training and know-how, subject to applicable regulatory and export-control requirements; and
coordinated engagement with government, defence-industry and prospective customers.

The parties will also cooperate in identifying and pursuing suitable commercial opportunities, including customer demonstrations, tender and procurement processes, government and defence-industry engagement and participation in major industry events.
Nexus 20 Platform in Poland

A Nexus 20 platform is already located in Poland and is intended to serve as an important technical demonstration, evaluation and market-development asset. Under the MOU, the parties intend to cooperate on engineering access, equipment integration, technical familiarisation, approved demonstrations and subsequent deployment opportunities.

The parties also intend to establish a joint working group to coordinate technical, industrial and commercial activities, maintain an implementation roadmap, monitor agreed milestones and support engagement with customers, government and the defence industry.
Pathway to Definitive Agreements
The MOU establishes a pathway toward the negotiation and execution of three definitive commercial agreements:
1. Sales and Marketing Agreement
To govern the promotion, marketing and sale of Nexus 20 platforms and associated products and services in agreed territories and customer segments.
2. Manufacturing Agreement

To govern the localisation, manufacture, assembly, integration and testing of Nexus 20 platforms in Poland, including manufacturing responsibilities, technology transfer, local sourcing, production readiness and quality requirements.
3. Maintenance and Support Agreement
To establish local capability for maintenance, repair, technical support, spare parts, training and lifecycle sustainment of Nexus 20 platforms.
CiTech Chief Executive Officer Brenton Scott said:
“The execution of this MOU is an important milestone in CiTech’s European strategy and moves our relationship with WZM and HCP from initial cooperation toward a structured industrial partnership.

“Poland is a strategically important defence and industrial market, with strong engineering capability and a central role in supporting security across NATO’s Eastern Flank. Working with established Polish industrial partners provides CiTech with a pathway to localise the manufacture, integration and lifecycle support of Nexus 20 while remaining close to our end customers.

“Importantly, this partnership is about more than market access. Our objective is to establish a sustainable Polish capability around Nexus 20, including manufacturing, integration, technical support, training and local supply-chain participation.

“With a Nexus 20 platform already in Poland, we are now positioned to progress technical engagement, demonstrations and industrialisation planning while working toward the definitive commercial agreements contemplated by the MOU.”
Next Steps

The parties intend to progress through a phased implementation program covering technical engagement, market demonstrations, industrialisation planning and negotiation of the three definitive agreements.
The MOU is intended to guide cooperation while the definitive agreements are negotiated.

About Wojskowe Zakłady Motoryzacyjne S.A.

Wojskowe Zakłady Motoryzacyjne S.A. (WZM) is a major Polish defence-industry company based in Poznań, Poland, with more than 80 years of experience supporting military vehicles. Founded in 1945, the company has evolved from a military vehicle repair organisation into a specialised industrial centre focused particularly on tracked armoured platforms, tanks, powerpacks and through-life support for the Polish Armed Forces.
www.wzm.eu/en
About H. Cegielski – Poznan S.A.

Founded in 1846, HCP is a Polish industrial and engineering company specialising in large-scale mechanical manufacturing, defence production, and industrial solutions. A subsidiary of Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa S.A. (PGZ), HCP provides advanced fabrication, machining, and integration capabilities for defence, energy, and transport sectors.
www.hcp.eu/en
About Critical Infrastructure Technologies Ltd.

Listed on the CSE with operations in Perth, Western Australia, CiTech is creating autonomous, high capacity, rapidly deployable technology that delivers essential services to where they are needed most. CiTech is targeting the mining, defence, border security/surveillance and emergency services sectors in relation to its first product release, the Nexus 16, which aims to provide critical mobile telecommunications for such sectors. Using patented technologies, CiTech’s self-deploying platform (SDP) provides a solution for two of the greatest limitations of current rapidly deployable communication solutions, strength of the tower and ability to rapidly self-deploy and operate, in numerous situations. The SDP is designed to support radio equipment including LTE (Long Term Evolution) and several other technological payloads, such as surveillance and anti-drone systems. CiTech has completed the research and development phase and is currently commercialising the first of many products that will be released. To learn more about the Company, visit www.citech.com.au.
